text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- As air traffic controllers end a week's go-slow, workers at the meteorological department step up their protest saying they will not release any weather data until their grievances are addressed.
- Exiled politician Sheikh Balala accuses the Kenyan and German governments of colluding to delay his return home until after the next general election in Kenya.
- A 1996 report published by the International Commission of Jurists (Kenya Chapter) accuses the Kenyan government of not being committed to democracy and pluralism.
- Kenyan dissident Koigi wa Wamwere, freed on bail on Friday, appeals to the government to allow him to enjoy his freedom like any other Kenyan.
- The levy on fishermen and swimmers outside designated reserves in the Indian Ocean abolished.
- Ian Gorst Johns, a tourism representative, says Kenya is losing it's lure as a tourist destination because the holiday package offered has not changed in 15 years.

- A district commissioner (administrator) in Kericho (Rift Valley) calls for drastic measures to contain the spread of AIDS following the death of six senior civil servants from the disease, which has paralysed some services in the district.
